name: Zoom Clinical Notes vs Freed
title: Zoom Clinical Notes vs Freed: AI Scribe Comparison for Telehealth
description: Compare Zoom Clinical Notes and Freed AI scribes. See differences in pricing, telehealth integration, EHR support, and features.

summary.bottom_line: Zoom Clinical Notes is seamlessly integrated with Zoom telehealth but requires enterprise pricing. Freed is more affordable ($39-119/mo) and works with any telehealth platform including Zoom, Doxy.me, and in-person visits. Choose Zoom Clinical Notes if you're all-in on Zoom healthcare; choose Freed for flexibility and transparent pricing.

key_differences.in_person_support: Both (Freed via mobile, Zoom via mobile)

sections.heading: Zoom Clinical Notes vs Freed: Overview
sections.content: Zoom Clinical Notes and Freed are both AI-powered documentation tools, but they take different approaches. Zoom Clinical Notes is built into Zoom's healthcare platform, designed for organizations already using Zoom for telehealth. It generates notes in under 60 seconds with 100+ specialty templates. Freed is an independent AI scribe that works with any telehealth platform (including Zoom) and offers more accessible pricing for solo practitioners and small practices. Both support in-person visits via mobile devices.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Freed has transparent public pricing: Starter ($39/mo, 40 notes), Core ($79/mo, unlimited), and Premier ($119/mo, EHR push + ICD-10). Zoom Clinical Notes does not publish pricing—it requires a Zoom Workplace for Clinicians license plus the Clinical Notes add-on, with custom enterprise quotes. Industry average for AI scribes is $150-200/provider/month, suggesting Zoom may be in that range. For solo practitioners, Freed is more accessible; for Zoom-committed organizations, bundled pricing may make sense.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: Both offer similar core features: ambient listening, fast note generation, ICD-10 coding, patient instructions, and referral letters. Zoom Clinical Notes is deeply integrated with Zoom telehealth—notes appear in a side panel during calls. Freed works across platforms via browser extension and offers native EHR push on Premier (Athenahealth, SimplePractice, etc.). Zoom has 100+ specialty templates; Freed has specialty-specific templates with custom template builder. Freed's platform flexibility is the key differentiator.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your telehealth platform and organization type:

recommendations.when: Your organization is committed to Zoom for Healthcare, you want seamless in-call documentation, or you're an enterprise negotiating bundled Zoom licensing
You're a solo practitioner or small practice, want transparent pricing, use multiple telehealth platforms (not just Zoom), or prefer trying before committing (7-day free trial)
You use Doxy.me, SimplePractice telehealth, or other platforms—Freed works across all while Zoom Clinical Notes is Zoom-only

faqs.q: Can I use Zoom Clinical Notes without Zoom for Healthcare?
faqs.a: No, Zoom Clinical Notes requires a Zoom Workplace for Clinicians license. It's not available as a standalone product. Practices not using Zoom for telehealth should consider Freed or other platform-agnostic AI scribes.

faqs.q: Does Freed work with Zoom telehealth?
faqs.a: Yes, Freed works with Zoom telehealth via browser extension. It also works with Doxy.me, and virtually any browser-based telehealth platform, giving more flexibility than Zoom Clinical Notes.

faqs.q: Which is better for solo practitioners?
faqs.a: Freed is more accessible for solo practitioners with transparent pricing starting at $39/month and a free trial. Zoom Clinical Notes is enterprise-focused without public pricing, making it harder for solo practitioners to evaluate and access.
Yes, both support in-person visits using mobile devices to capture ambient audio. Zoom Clinical Notes works via the Zoom mobile app; Freed has its own mobile app for in-person documentation.
